verdict: Reddit's revenue jumped 61% to $805M as its ad business caught fire — and with costs growing far more slowly, net income more than doubled to $253M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted — more than double a year ago

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's communities — powered by more users, more time on site, and better ad targeting.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Mostly data licensing — deals that let AI companies train on Reddit's public posts — plus Reddit Premium subscriptions.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the product and the ad platform — up 18% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning advertisers and users — up 62% YoY, the fastest-growing cost line.

otherDetail: Other income of $25M, net — mostly interest earned on Reddit's $2.8B pile of cash and marketable securities.

takeaways.title: Eight straight quarters above 60%
takeaways.text: Revenue growth stayed above 60% for the eighth consecutive quarter, driven by ads (+64%). International revenue grew even faster, +84% to $167M.

takeaways.title: Half a billion weekly users
takeaways.text: Daily active uniques rose 18% to 130.3 million, and weekly users crossed half a billion at 514.6 million — more audience for the ad machine to sell.

takeaways.title: Profit is scaling faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Net income more than doubled to $253M — 31% of revenue — because revenue grew 61% while total costs grew about a third. Reddit also bought back $235M of its own stock.

footerNote: Figures are rounded to the nearest $M, following the same convention as Reddit's Q3 2026 page; the statements report in thousands.
